articles.title: Could one amino acid help explain why men tend to live shorter lives?
articles.description: A UK Biobank cohort and Mendelian randomization study involving 272,475 participants linked higher circulating tyrosine with greater all-cause mortality and genetically predicted higher tyrosine with shorter lifespan. After accounting for phenylalanine, the relationship with shorter lifespan was clearest in men, while findings in women were less consistent, suggesting a potential sex-specific role for tyrosine in longevity.

articles.title: Study reveals evolutionary advantage of human heel-first walking style
